finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST to import.php makes the server fetch an attacker-supplied URL via file_get_contents; response length is echoed back. Severity HIGH: anonymous remote user, no allowlist, no scheme or IP restriction, redirects followed. Response body is not returned, only its length (length oracle for internal port/file probing; IMDSv1 metadata reachable; IMDSv2 mitigated because the token header cannot be sent). Assumes PHP allow_url_fopen is on (unconfirmed; config not in repo). Validation tier 0.

trace.note: POST branch taken when feed is set; no session or admin check precedes it
file_get_contents fetches the raw caller value; follows HTTP redirects by default
strlen of response echoed to the caller (length oracle)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme restriction (http, https, file, and other stream wrappers accepted); no hostname allowlist; no RFC-1918, loopback, or link-local IP block; no post-redirect re-validation; no authentication. Only the echo of length, not the body, limits the impact.

verdict.reason: import.php:11 takes the POST branch on any request with `feed` set and no session or admin check, `file_get_contents($_POST['feed'])` at import.php:12 fetches the raw attacker value, and import.php:13 echoes only strlen; `require_admin()` (import.php:4-9) guards only the `set_webhook` branch at line 18, so nothing validates the URL on this path. The PHP allow_url_fopen setting is unverified from the repo, but that affects only whether the fetch works, not whether the finding is refuted.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: an authenticated admin session can make the server send a request to an arbitrary URL via curl. Response is discarded. Severity MEDIUM: admin precondition and blind response. Admin status does not close SSRF to internal ranges. Not verified: where is_admin is set.

trace.note: require_admin() checks $_SESSION['is_admin'] and exits 403 if empty
curl_init called with the raw value; no allowlist
curl_exec dispatches the request; response discarded, 'ok' returned

finding.guards_checked: Admin session gate (require_admin, is_admin set outside this file, not verified); no hostname allowlist; no scheme restriction (CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS not set); no IP block; CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION unset so no redirects followed.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:18 (defined import.php:4-9) exits 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is set. The only is_admin reference in the directory is that check (import.php:5), so where admin is granted is not in this code.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file (import.php:18-22), but the source fails the check: $_POST['set_webhook'] reaches curl_init only after require_admin() at import.php:18 has confirmed an admin session, so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control it. The finding is an admin-only SSRF, not one reachable by a low-privilege remote attacker.
